Who collects delinquent property tax in Nassau County, NY?

The Nassau County Treasurer collects delinquent tax for the whole county at 1 West Street in Mineola, and the phone number on the county page is 516-571-2090. Hours are 9:00 am to 4:30 pm, Monday through Friday. Current bills are handled by the receiver of taxes in your town, but once a balance turns delinquent it moves to the county's Tax Records unit.

The scope depends on where you live. For the Towns of Hempstead, North Hempstead and Oyster Bay, the Treasurer takes both general and school delinquencies. The City of Glen Cove handles its own school tax delinquencies, so only its general tax comes to the county, and for the City of Long Beach the county takes school tax plus only the county portion of the general tax.

  • Delinquent school tax collection starts June 1; delinquent general tax collection starts September 1.
  • Always write the parcel section, block and lot on any check.
  • Checks go to the Nassau County Treasurer, 1 West Street, Mineola, NY 11501, or into the lobby drop-box.

What are the 2026 delinquent tax payment deadlines in Nassau County?

For 2026 delinquent taxes, the county lists personal checks accepted from June 1 through November 30, 2026, and online credit card or electronic check payments from June 26, 2026 through January 31, 2027. The last day to pay before the lien sale is Wednesday, February 10, 2027 at 3:00 PM.

Online payments carry small charges. The Treasurer's page cites $0.45 for an electronic check and a 2.3% bank charge for a credit card. The ACH limit is $99,999.99 and the card limit is $25,000. Tax liens already sold are different: they cannot be paid online and need a bank cashier's check or cash.

How does the Nassau County tax lien sale work?

Instead of foreclosing right away, Nassau County sells its unpaid tax liens each February at a public online auction. On February 16, 2027 the Treasurer will sell the 2026 liens on parcels whose balance has not been paid by February 10.

Source: Nassau County Annual Tax Lien Sale. A bidder who misses the 90% balance deadline forfeits winning bids and the deposit. The Treasurer's office also refunds tax certiorari awards and settlements, which is the money side of a successful assessment appeal. Bidders pay a $175 registration fee and a $5,000 minimum deposit, then 10% of the purchase is due the day of the sale and the remaining 90% by March 18. If you own a parcel on the list, February 10 is the date that matters most to you.

How do I appeal a Nassau County assessment?

Nassau County appeals go to the Assessment Review Commission, which is independent of the Department of Assessment, and the next filing window runs from January 4, 2027 to March 1, 2027. The county says no fee is charged to file for yourself, and the Commission can lower an assessment or leave it as is, but it cannot raise it.

Timing of the effect is slower than many owners expect. Assessments published in January become final on the first business day of April of the following year, and they feed school tax bills in October of that year and general tax bills in the January after that. A reduction won now therefore reaches your bill well after you file, and a seller who closes first may leave the benefit to the buyer.

Filing is online through AROW, and the county recommends it over paper. The Commission's questions line is 516-571-3214. Three forms exist: AR1 for a one-, two- or three-family home, AR2 for other property, and AR3 for tax class or exemption disputes. Appeals take up to fifteen months, with determinations by March 31 of the year after you file.

  • Class 1 homes cannot see a total assessment rise more than 6% in a year or 20% in five years, except for construction or renovation.
  • Village, Glen Cove and Long Beach assessments are appealed locally, and an ARC filing does not protect those rights.
  • If you reject an offered reduction, owner-occupied homes can pursue small claims review after the final roll on the first business day of April.

What does the Nassau County housing market mean for a tax-owing seller?

Nassau County is dense and expensive. Census estimates for July 2025 show 1,398,939 residents across 284.54 square miles of land, with 480,591 housing units. Owners occupy 81.9% of homes, the median owner-occupied value is $684,700 for 2020 to 2024, and median household income is $146,202.

Median gross rent is $2,252, the average household has 2.99 people, and 23.3% of residents were born outside the United States. The county was formed in 1899 from Queens County, has Mineola as its seat, and is divided into two cities, three towns and 64 incorporated villages. It also has 58 public school districts, whose boundaries do not match village or postal lines. That patchwork explains why two houses on the same street can carry different school bills.

For a seller with a delinquent bill, the date matters most. A sale that fails to close before February 10 leaves the 2026 lien exposed to the February 16 auction.

What are my options if I owe Nassau County tax and want to sell?

Request the current balance by parcel from the Treasurer and see whether your lien has been sold already. The Treasurer's unpaid tax listings page carries monthly updated delinquent tax files. A sale that closes before February 10 pays the balance from proceeds, which stops the lien from going to auction.

A buyer paying cash and taking the house as it is can close faster than a financed buyer, and speed is what protects you against the lien-sale calendar. If you think your assessment is too high, filing with ARC in early 2027 can reduce the next bill whether or not you sell, and a pending sale does not prevent you from filing.

  1. Get a payoff in writing from the Treasurer, 516-571-2090.
  2. Check whether your parcel is in a village, Glen Cove or Long Beach, since delinquent tax rules differ there.
  3. Set a closing date before February 10, 2027 if the 2026 tax is still open.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I pay delinquent taxes in Nassau County?

Pay the Nassau County Treasurer, either online at the county's delinquent tax page or by check to 1 West Street, Mineola, NY 11501. Include your parcel section, block and lot. Help with online payments is at 516-571-2090.

What is the last day to pay 2026 delinquent tax before the lien sale?

Wednesday, February 10, 2027, at 3:00 PM. The lien auction itself is on February 16, 2027, and the county will sell the 2026 liens on any parcels that remain unpaid.

When can I appeal my Nassau County assessment?

From January 4, 2027 through March 1, 2027, through the Assessment Review Commission's online AROW system or on paper. The county states that no extension is available after March 1.

Can the Assessment Review Commission raise my assessment?

No. It can reduce the assessment or leave it unchanged. Filing yourself costs nothing, and you do not have to hire a representative.

Does Nassau County foreclose directly on unpaid tax?

The county's page describes an annual tax lien sale each February, where liens on unpaid taxes are sold at online auction. Ask the Treasurer how a sold lien is handled for your parcel.

Which office collects Suffolk County property tax?

A Receiver of Taxes in each of the ten towns collects Suffolk County's combined town, school and county bill from December 1 through May 31, and the County Comptroller collects whatever is still unpaid after that. The ten towns are Babylon, Brookhaven, East Hampton, Huntington, Islip, Riverhead, Shelter Island, Smithtown, Southampton and Southold. Your town Assessor sets the assessed value, and the Receiver in your town issues the bill.

Suffolk is the easternmost county in New York and takes up the eastern two-thirds of Long Island. The county seat is Riverhead, though most county offices are in Hauppauge. It was one of twelve original counties created in 1683. The Comptroller's collection office is at 330 Center Drive, Riverhead, NY 11901, with administrative hours that start at 9:00 a.m. and finish at five in the afternoon, and counter payments ending at 4:15 p.m. The main number is 631-852-3000.

  • Town Receiver of Taxes: bills, duplicate bills and payments through May 31.
  • Town Assessor: value, exemptions and mailing-address changes.
  • County Comptroller: delinquent tax, bankruptcies, refunds of overpayment, tax liens and redemption statements.

Which Suffolk County towns have the most homes to tax?

Brookhaven is the largest of the ten towns by a wide margin, followed by Islip, Babylon, Huntington and Smithtown. The county's town list shows these populations:

  • Brookhaven: 488,497
  • Islip: 337,922
  • Babylon: 217,656
  • Huntington: 203,243
  • Smithtown: 115,768
  • Riverhead: 35,834
  • East Hampton: 28,607
  • Southold: 23,912
  • Southampton: 69,490
  • Shelter Island: 3,276

Suffolk also has 32 incorporated villages, from Amityville and Babylon to Sag Harbor and Westhampton Beach. The county also lists dozens of school districts, among them Brentwood, Commack, Half Hollow Hills and Hampton Bays. Ask your town Receiver which town, school and other levies make up the bill for your parcel.

What is the Suffolk County tax year and when is the bill due?

The tax year runs December 1 to November 30 of the following year, and bills are mailed by the town Receivers around mid-December. Pay the first half by January 10 to avoid interest. After that, 1 percent a month applies to the first half until May 31. The second half is payable without interest through May 31.

One detail trips up people who buy in spring. Suffolk's own notice tells anyone who buys property during the year to find out whether the second-half tax has been paid, because the new owner is the one who has to deal with it. Another is that exemptions granted to the previous owner, such as a veterans or senior exemption, do not pass to the buyer, so the first bill after a sale can be much higher.

Partial payments of at least $200 are accepted by both the Receiver and the Comptroller. Interest and penalties are charged on the unpaid balance only, and accepting a partial payment does not waive the County's lien rights on what remains.

What happens to Suffolk taxes unpaid after May 31?

They become delinquent, payable to the County Comptroller, with a 5 percent penalty and interest of 1 percent a month counted from February 1 on the tax plus penalty. A tax sale advertising fee is added to anything still unpaid after August 31. The Comptroller's own example shows a $1,000 tax growing to $1,050 with the penalty and to $1,102.50 if paid by June 30.

Mail a delinquent payment to the Suffolk County Comptroller, 330 Center Drive, Riverhead, NY 11901, with the property description exactly as it reads on the tax bill or deed.

Does Suffolk County take the house if the tax stays unpaid?

Not at once. If tax is still unpaid on the date of the lien sale, usually held in November or December, the Comptroller sells the County a tax lien against the parcel. Before that sale, the list of liens runs for six weeks in the official newspapers and for two weeks in a newspaper in each of the ten towns.

After the sale the owner can clear the lien by paying the lien amount, accrued interest and any later County taxes through an application to the Comptroller. The window is twelve months from the sale date, and thirty-six months if the parcel is assessed as a one-, two- or three-family residence. Redemption statements covering every open lien are available from the Comptroller on request.

When the period runs out the County issues a tax deed. Redeeming after that point means applying to the Suffolk County Department of Planning, Division of Real Estate, at 631-853-5900. The Comptroller's contact page lists that same number for redemption of property taken by tax deed.

What should I do after buying a house or paying off a mortgage in Suffolk?

Contact your local Receiver of Taxes right away. The County says a new owner should get a current bill and learn what is due next and when. An owner who has just satisfied a mortgage with taxes in escrow should ask the Receiver to send future bills straight to the owner, then confirm the next payment date and mailing address.

  • Ask whether the second-half tax on the parcel has been paid.
  • Ask the Assessor to correct the mailing address, since the Assessor drives the roll that bills come from.
  • Check whether a bank paid the whole year when a mortgage ended mid-year. The bank is not obliged to forward a bill.
  • Keep records of any exemption you hope to claim by March 1.

For refunds of overpaid tax, bankruptcy questions and court-ordered reductions or corrections of error, the Comptroller's office uses the same main number, 631-852-3000.

Where do I dispute a Suffolk County assessment?

Bring your complaint to your town's review board on Grievance Day, the third Tuesday in May, which is May 18 in 2027. The board must sit for at least four hours. The county assessment calendar the Comptroller publishes runs in this order:

  • January 1: valuation date.
  • March 1: taxable status date, and the deadline for all exemption filings.
  • Third Tuesday in May: Grievance Day.
  • July 1: final roll, with taxes extended from it.

If the board does not give you relief, a small claims petition has a 30-day clock that starts when the final roll is filed. To qualify you need to have filed a written complaint with the Board of Assessment Review and live in a one-, two- or three-family house used only as a residence. Your town Assessor, not the County, holds the assessment file.

What do Suffolk County housing numbers look like for a seller?

Suffolk is expensive and owner-heavy. Census QuickFacts for 2020-2024 put the median home value at $578,400, with 82.2 percent of homes lived in by their owners, across 512,565 households. Median household income is $130,686, and renters pay a median of $2,255 in gross rent. The county estimate for July 2025 is 1,546,090 people, up from 1,525,920 at the 2020 census.

Geography shapes risk. The county covers 2,373 square miles, of which only 912 are land, with roughly 980 miles of coastline and a high point of 401 feet at Jayne's Hill. Because so much of the housing sits near sea level, buyers often ask for flood and drainage history. Pull your insurance records and any elevation certificate before you list.

Frequently asked questions

Who do I pay Suffolk County property tax to before May 31?

The Receiver of Taxes in your town. Taxes are payable there from December 1 to May 31, and after that date they go to the County Comptroller.

How long can I redeem a Suffolk County tax lien?

Twelve months from the lien sale, or thirty-six months for a one-, two- or three-family residence. After that the County issues a tax deed.

Is a mailed Suffolk tax payment accepted by postmark?

Yes, by the USPS postmark on the envelope. A metered postmark is not accepted, so use certified or registered mail near a deadline.

What if I never received my Suffolk County tax bill?

You still owe the tax plus any penalty and interest. Ask your town Receiver of Taxes for a duplicate bill right away.

Does a Suffolk tax exemption move to the buyer of my house?

No. A veterans or senior exemption stays with the person who received it, so the buyer's first tax bill can be higher than yours was.

Who collects property tax in Westchester County, NY?

Your city or town collects it, and the county does not. The Westchester County Tax Commission says plainly that the county takes no property tax payments directly from owners and asks people not to mail it checks. The 25 cities and towns also bill and collect the county's share, then guarantee and forward the total to the county's Finance Department.

Westchester covers six cities, 19 towns and 23 villages in the Hudson Valley, with White Plains as the county seat. Yonkers is the largest municipality. Because bills, assessment records and tax history all live at the local level, the first call about a bill always goes to the municipality where the house sits.

  • City or town receiver of taxes: bills, payments, balances and payoff letters.
  • Local assessor: value, exemptions and name changes.
  • County Finance Department, 148 Martine Avenue, White Plains: county tax refunds after a small claims reduction. The Commissioner of Finance is also the county treasurer.
  • County Tax Commission, 110 Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd., Room L-346, White Plains, phone 914-995-4325: general property tax questions and equalization data.

What does the Westchester County Tax Commission do?

It spreads the county levy fairly among the municipalities and trains local assessment staff. The Commission reviews local assessment rolls each year for that purpose, orients new assessors, trains Board of Assessment Review members, reviews applications to correct tax and assessment errors, and publishes an annual report on assessments, equalization, exemptions and tax rates.

The Commission does not set individual assessments, collect current or delinquent tax, or take part in lien sales and foreclosure. Those jobs belong to the towns, cities and villages. The county describes its own property taxes as among the highest in the nation, which is one reason local grievance deadlines matter to a seller.

When are Westchester property taxes due?

The date depends on the municipality, and the county publishes a chart of the last day to pay without penalty. County tax is due once a year in April, May or June in most of the cities below, and Peekskill splits it in two, while city, town and school bills follow their own calendars. A village adds a fourth bill in some places.

Who runs tax lien sales in Westchester County?

The city or town where the property sits runs them, since the county Finance Department states that it does not conduct delinquent property tax lien sales. The cities and towns also pursue collection against owners who fall behind, so a balance that looks old can still be enforced locally.

State law gives the outline for a delinquent parcel. A lien can be redeemed by paying the amount due plus legal charges, and the redemption period under RPTL 1110 ends two years after the lien date unless a notice or a local choice changes it. Legal charges can include notice costs, interest and penalties, and an allowance of up to $250 or 2 percent of the amount due on a parcel, whichever is greater, under RPTL 1102.

Local rules differ. Yonkers charges 15 percent annual interest from the confirmation date with no grace period, and White Plains charges 1 percent a month on overdue tax. Ask the municipality that holds your lien what its sale schedule is, and whether any notices have been mailed.

How does a Westchester small claims reduction turn into a refund?

After you win a Small Claim Assessment Review in court, your municipality has to complete a county refund form, and the county aims to process its portion within 90 days after it has all the paperwork. The form needs signatures from the assessor and the receiver of taxes, plus a copy of the court decision or the settlement signed by the hearing officer.

The municipality mails the package to the County Finance Department, Attn: SCAR Processing, 148 Martine Avenue, Suite 724, White Plains, NY 10601. The refund check goes to the owner's address, or to the address on the court order. The county says it cannot process incomplete paperwork, and it can speak only to the county portion of the refund. Ask your city, town or school district about refunds of local tax.

The tool is meant for residential owners. If you plan to sell, tell the title company about any pending SCAR result and ask who receives a refund that arrives after closing.

What do Census figures say about Westchester County homes?

1,015,743 residents for July 2025 and 399,598 housing units. About 61.8 percent of households own their home. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $663,200 for 2020 to 2024, and median household income is $118,976.

Owners with a mortgage pay a median of $4,000 a month, and median gross rent is $1,951. The county averages 2,332 people per square mile across 430.72 square miles of land, and 34.8 percent of residents age five and over speak a language other than English at home. Because the county mixes dense cities with large-lot suburbs, a median value tells you little about your own street. Look at recent nearby sales.

Corporate headquarters in the county include IBM, Mastercard, PepsiCo and Regeneron, according to the county's Wikipedia entry, and the Bronx River Parkway, completed in 1925, was the first modern multi-lane limited-access road in North America.

What should I check before selling a Westchester County house with tax due?

Request a payoff from the city or town receiver of taxes, since that office holds the combined county, local and school figures. Then work through a short list.

  • Find out which installments are paid and which are open, including school tax.
  • Ask whether the bill is on a lien list and whether a sale or redemption deadline is coming.
  • Ask for the exact payoff date that interest runs to.
  • Check whether a Small Claim Assessment Review or a certiorari case is pending on the parcel.
  • Confirm the owner name and mailing address on the assessment roll.

A cash buyer can close with these balances open, and the title company pays them from your proceeds at the table. What you net depends on the payoff amounts, so get them in writing.

Frequently asked questions

Do I pay Westchester County property tax to the county?

No. You pay your city or town, which also bills the county's share. The county's Tax Commission asks owners not to mail property tax checks to the county.

Does Westchester County sell tax liens?

No. The County Finance Department says it does not run delinquent tax lien sales. The city or town where the property sits conducts them.

Where do I send paperwork for a Westchester small claims refund?

Your municipality sends it to County Finance, Attn: SCAR Processing, 148 Martine Avenue, Suite 724, White Plains, NY 10601. You do not mail the county form yourself.

How can I find a Westchester city's tax dates?

Use the county's chart of property tax payment dates, which lists the last day to pay without penalty for each municipality. Yonkers dates vary with the City Council's levy date, so confirm with the city's tax office.

Who can answer questions about Westchester equalization rates?

The County Tax Commission in White Plains, phone 914-995-4325. It publishes equalization tables and historical rates, and its page invites questions about county property taxes and exemptions.

Who collects property tax in Rockland County?

A town receiver collects the first payment, and the County Department of Finance takes over any unpaid balance on April 1. Rockland County has five towns, so the receiver you pay in January depends on whether your house is in Clarkstown, Haverstraw, Orangetown, Ramapo or Stony Point.

The county seat is New City, and the county is the smallest in New York outside New York City by area, with about 173.55 square miles of land. It also counts eighteen incorporated villages inside those towns, and nearly a third of its area is parkland. That mix of towns and villages explains why two neighbors can have different assessors and different local bills even though the county collection rules are the same.

The Department of Finance sits at 50 Sanatorium Road, Building A, 8th Floor, Pomona, NY 10970. The main number is (845) 364-3870, and the tax unit answers at (845) 364-3877. Office hours on the department's contact page are Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

How does the Rockland quarterly payment plan work?

Owners can split the combined county and town tax into four payments with a 5 percent service charge, and the first of the four is due January 15 to the town receiver. The second, third and fourth payments go to the Commissioner of Finance.

The county tax division page attaches firm consequences to the plan:

  • Miss any quarterly payment and the whole unpaid balance becomes due at once.
  • A 5 percent penalty is added to that balance, with interest of 1 percent per month until it is paid.
  • Only certain towns offer the plan, so ask your receiver whether yours does before you count on it.

An owner who skips the plan and has not paid the receiver by March 31 sees the account transferred to the Commissioner of Finance on April 1. From that date the payment goes to Pomona, not to the town hall.

What are the key Rockland County tax dates?

The county's dates cluster in the first half of the year, with the January 15 receiver payment and the April 1 transfer to the Commissioner doing most of the work for a delinquent account.

Quarterly payments two through four are made to the Commissioner of Finance and may be paid through the county's online system. Call (845) 364-3877 or (845) 364-3878 for details of an installment agreement, which can be paid off in full at any time.

How do I pay overdue Rockland County tax?

Pay online with an electronic check, which costs nothing, or by credit card, which carries a 3 percent fee. You can also mail a check, certified funds or a money order payable to the Commissioner of Finance.

The mailing address is Commissioner of Finance, 50 Sanatorium Road, Bldg. A, 8th Floor, Pomona, NY 10970. The county's finance page says tax searches and duplicate receipts are available by calling the tax office, and it advises calling for an updated payoff figure when an amount is in question. Because interest keeps running at 1 percent a month on a defaulted balance, a figure from last month can be wrong.

Does Rockland County foreclose on unpaid property tax?

Yes. The county's example on its tax page is that taxes for 2010 would be subject to foreclosure around June 2012, which is about two years after the tax year. The Department of Finance also runs auctions of county-owned property acquired through foreclosure.

Its most recent notice scheduled a public auction of county-owned tax delinquent property for March 12, 2026 at 7:00 p.m. in the Legislative Chambers of the Allison-Parris County Office Building, 11 New Hempstead Road, New City. That date has passed, so look for the next notice on the finance page.

New York law gives a delinquent tax lien a two-year redemption period, with a district allowed to extend it for homes, under RPTL section 1110. The practical message for a Rockland owner is to act while the account is still with the town receiver or in its first year with the county, and call the tax unit about an installment agreement before the account ages further.

Who sets and reviews the assessment on a Rockland house?

The assessor in your own town does, not the county. The county's tax page tells owners with an assessment question to contact the assessor's office in the town where they live.

That means a Haverstraw owner and an Orangetown owner file with different offices and may face different dates. Ask your town assessor for its grievance date and exemption deadlines. For a sale, the practical step is to pull the current assessed value and any exemptions from the town, because the county only collects what the town rolls produce.

Rockland County's Department of Finance does not set values. Its role is the money side: collection of delinquent taxes, tax searches, and the auction of properties the county has acquired.

What happens to a Rockland County tax bill when I sell?

The title company asks the county or the town receiver for a tax search and pays any open balance from the sale proceeds at closing, so owing tax does not prevent a sale. The balance simply reduces what you take home.

Two steps help a closing go smoothly. First, find out whether the account is still with the town receiver or has gone to the Commissioner of Finance, since that decides which office issues the payoff. Second, if you were using the quarterly plan, ask for the remaining balance with the 5 percent service charge included, because the plan's charges attach to the account.

A buyer paying cash for a house as it stands still needs those figures, and having a written payoff on hand before the contract is signed keeps the closing date from slipping.

What do Census numbers show about Rockland County housing?

Rockland County is expensive and mostly owner-occupied: the Census Bureau's QuickFacts table shows an owner-occupied rate of 67.9 percent and a median home value of $596,900 for 2020-2024. The July 2025 population estimate is 357,397, up 5.6 percent from the April 2020 base.

  • Housing units: 109,999.
  • Households: 103,879, averaging 3.22 people each, one of the larger household sizes in the state.
  • Median gross rent: $1,901.
  • Median household income: $109,959.
  • Median monthly owner costs with a mortgage: $3,641.
  • Building permits in 2025: 429.

Commuters reach New York City by the Palisades Parkway, the Thruway, NJ Transit and Metro-North rail on the Port Jervis and Pascack Valley lines, and a ferry connection at Haverstraw.

Frequently asked questions

Which office do I call about Rockland County property tax?

The Department of Finance tax unit at (845) 364-3877, or the main line at (845) 364-3870. For a value or exemption question, call the assessor in your own town.

When does Rockland turn unpaid tax over to the county?

April 1. If the receiver has not been paid by March 31, the account goes to the Commissioner of Finance on April 1.

Is there a fee for paying Rockland tax by card?

Yes, 3 percent for a credit card. An electronic check through the same online system has no charge.

What happens if I miss a quarterly payment in Rockland?

The whole unpaid balance comes due immediately with a 5 percent penalty and 1 percent interest per month. Call the tax unit before that happens to ask about an installment agreement.

Can I sell my Rockland house with unpaid tax?

Yes. The balance is paid out of your proceeds at closing, and the Commissioner of Finance or the town receiver supplies the payoff figure.

Where is Orange County, New York, and what does it include?

Orange County lies in the Hudson Valley, northwest of New York City, with Goshen as the county seat. It is the only New York county that touches both the Hudson and Delaware Rivers, and the only one that borders both New Jersey and Pennsylvania. The county has three cities, Middletown, Newburgh and Port Jervis, and it is split into 20 towns with a scattering of villages.

The land is varied. The Shawangunk Ridge marks the western edge, the Hudson Highlands run along the Rockland County line and south of Newburgh, and the Wallkill River valley fills the middle. In the south that valley opens into the Black Dirt Region, a former glacial lake bed known for farm soil. The county covers about 840 square miles and was created in 1683, then reorganized with its present boundaries in 1798.

Interstate 84, the Thruway (Interstate 87), Route 17 and the Palisades Parkway are the main roads. Stewart International Airport sits near Newburgh, and the Port Jervis Line of Metro-North serves the western end.

Who collects property tax in Orange County?

Town, county and special district bills are mailed by the town and paid to the town collector without penalty during the collection window. Delinquent amounts and penalties go to the county Department of Finance, now on the third floor of the County Building at 255 Main Street in Goshen. The county's page lists 845-291-2480 for questions.

Three cities are carved out. The county does not collect or enforce taxes inside Middletown, Newburgh or Port Jervis, so owners there deal with the city directly. Properties outside those cities but inside the Middletown, Newburgh or Port Jervis school districts pay current school tax to the district and only pay the county once the bill turns delinquent.

  • County and town tax: collected January through March.
  • School tax: collected September through November.
  • Village tax: collected June through October, with an earlier start in a few villages.
  • Delinquent school tax from outside-city parcels reaches the county in March for Middletown, April for Newburgh and November for Port Jervis, on the county's calendar.

How does the Orange County tax foreclosure auction work?

The county takes possession of parcels for unpaid tax through a foreclosure once a year, and the parcels are then offered at a public auction. A booklet with general information and the list of parcels is available from the Real Property Tax office before the sale. At this writing the county's auction page says no tax delinquency auctions are scheduled.

Parcels that do not sell go onto a leftover list that used to be open for bids each month, but the page says that deed sale process is paused because of recent changes to New York's Real Property Tax Law. Bids on the leftover list require official bank checks or money orders and a 10 percent deposit, not cash.

The county also posts surplus and non-surplus reports for the 2024 and 2025 auctions and the 2025 leftover list, which follow the state's Article 11 changes. The page tells anyone claiming surplus funds to consult an attorney. A seller who is behind should ask Finance how far the foreclosure has gone before choosing between paying, selling and waiting.

What is the grievance and relief process in Orange County?

Assessments in Orange County are set by the town or city assessor, so complaints go to the local board of assessment review. State law opens those hearings on the fourth Tuesday of May unless a local law sets another date, and the State Tax Department advises checking the date with your assessor. If the board leaves the value unchanged, Small Claims Assessment Review is the lower-cost court route for most homeowners, and a tax certiorari case in State Supreme Court is the route that calls for an attorney.

The county's parcel search lets you look up owner, assessed values, tax maps, photos and comparable sales for any parcel, and it is useful before a grievance and before pricing a sale. For state relief, the STAR credit is registered through the State Tax Department's Homeowner Benefit Portal, and a seller should close that registration at the sale.

What changes if my Orange County house is inside a village or a city?

A village adds its own bill. Owners in a village pay current and late village tax to the village itself up to October 31, so a village balance is not something to settle at the county office. Most villages mail bills in June, while South Blooming Grove and the Village of Kiryas mail in January and Cornwall-on-Hudson and Washingtonville mail in March.

City owners have their own offices. The county's collection page lists the City of Middletown at 845-346-4150, the City of Newburgh at 845-569-7330 and the City of Port Jervis at 845-858-4014. Each city's school district sets its own dates as well, and the three districts publish their own phone numbers for tax questions.

For a sale, this means several balances may sit on one house, such as town and county, village or city, and school. Ask the buyer's closing attorney to request each payoff separately, and match every figure to the day of closing so nothing is left behind on the next bill.

How do I sell an Orange County house that has tax due?

Work out which collector holds the balance. In a town, current bills sit with the town collector until the window closes and then move to the county Department of Finance. In Middletown, Newburgh or Port Jervis, call the city.

  • Ask for a payoff figure in writing, with the date it is good through.
  • Ask whether foreclosure has started on the parcel.
  • Give the figure to your attorney so it is paid at closing.
  • Close your STAR registration if you receive that benefit.

A buyer paying cash can purchase the house as it is, with the lien, any repairs and any tenants.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I pay delinquent property tax in Orange County, NY?

Delinquent county and town tax goes to the Orange County Department of Finance, on the third floor of the County Building at 255 Main Street in Goshen. The number on the county's pages is 845-291-2480. Inside the cities of Middletown, Newburgh and Port Jervis the county does not collect, so call the city.

When are Orange County property tax bills collected?

Collection periods vary by town, but county and town tax is generally collected January through March, school tax September through November and village tax June through October. Your own bill states the dates that apply, and your municipality's collector can confirm them.

Is the Orange County tax auction happening now?

The county's auction page currently states that no tax delinquency auctions are scheduled. It also says the leftover list deed sale is paused because of changes to state tax law. Sign up for the page's email alerts or ask the Real Property Tax office for updates.

What can I do if I think my Orange County assessment is too high?

File a complaint with your town or city board of assessment review, which meets starting the fourth Tuesday in May unless a local law sets another date. If that fails, Small Claims Assessment Review is open to most homeowners. Call your assessor first, since an informal talk can fix errors.

Can I sell my house in Orange County before foreclosure?

Yes. The county can only auction a parcel once foreclosure is complete, and a sale that pays the full tax lien at closing clears the debt. Ask Finance for a written payoff and which stage your parcel has reached, and do not wait for an auction notice.

Which Erie County office handles what on a property tax bill?

Erie County splits the work: city and town assessors set values, town tax receivers collect current bills, and the county's Real Property Tax Services (RPTS) office handles delinquent county tax and foreclosure. RPTS is in the Rath County Office Building, 95 Franklin Street, Room 100, Buffalo, NY 14202, and its tax line is (716) 858-8333. The county site lists assessors and town clerks and tax receivers under its General Information page, along with pages on contesting an assessment and the assessment calendar.

The county's Pay Your Taxes page says its online system takes current City of Buffalo county property taxes and delinquent Erie County taxes for any town or city in the county, and also lets you look up what is owed. If you live outside Buffalo, current tax goes to your town receiver, so ask the town clerk for the collection dates and penalty schedule, which differ by municipality.

The county Comptroller's office, at (716) 858-8400, holds surplus money left after a foreclosure auction pays the taxes and charges against a parcel.

How does Erie County foreclose on unpaid county tax?

The county can foreclose on a tax lien once it has been unpaid for two or more years, and it does so through a numbered in rem proceeding. Erie County's In Rem 173 notice says the county filed its List of Delinquent Taxes with the County Clerk on September 9, 2025, covering liens through tax year 2022. Redemption closed on November 10, 2025, and a statutory foreclosure fee of $500 had to accompany the unpaid liens.

A later round, In Rem 174, began on May 5, 2026. The county's auction page shows a Judgment of Foreclosure and Sale filed for it, and it announced a public auction for August 26, 2026 at the Buffalo Convention Center covering In Rem 172 and 173 properties only. That date has passed, so ask RPTS about the next sale schedule.

  • Pay with cash, certified check, bank check or money order. Personal checks are not accepted.
  • Interest is applied on the first day of each month, so the payoff figure changes monthly.
  • Paying the old liens does not stop later years from becoming eligible, so open 2023, 2024 and 2025 county taxes keep accruing interest and fees.
  • Payment plans may be available for certain residential, owner-occupied property, case by case.

The county warns that scammers target owners in foreclosure and says neither it nor its attorneys will ask for gift cards, cryptocurrency, wire transfers or online banking logins. Free help is available from the state Attorney General's Homeowner Protection Program at 1-855-HOME-456.

What does Erie County look like for homeowners?

Erie County covers 1,227 square miles on Lake Erie, of which 1,043 are land. Buffalo is the county seat and holds about 28% of the population. The northern half, known as the Northtowns, is flat and rises gently from the lake, while the Southtowns are hillier and reach the northwestern foothills of the Appalachians. Interstates 90, 190, 290 and 990 and US routes 20, 62 and 219 carry most of the traffic.

There are 16 villages in the county, including Williamsville, Hamburg, Kenmore, East Aurora and Orchard Park, and school districts range from Buffalo City to small central districts such as Holland and Akron. Tax bills therefore vary by town, village and district. The county was created in 1821 out of Niagara County, and Clarence and Willink were its first towns. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page gives the county-wide picture.

Interest is added on the first of every month, which makes the redemption date in each in rem notice worth marking on a calendar. Notices also go to mortgage holders and others with an interest in the parcel, and the county advises those recipients to speak with an attorney to protect their position.

Does STAR work differently in Buffalo than in the rest of Erie County?

Yes. The state's Types of STAR page says STAR applies only to school district taxes, with five cities as exceptions: New York, Buffalo, Rochester, Yonkers and Syracuse. In those cities the benefit is applied partly to city taxes and partly to school taxes. A Buffalo homeowner and a Lancaster homeowner can therefore see the benefit land on different lines of the bill.

The credit comes as a check or direct deposit. The older STAR exemption on the bill continues only for owners who have held it since 2015 on the same home, and new homeowners register for the credit. Basic STAR has a $500,000 income limit for the credit, and Enhanced STAR for owners aged 65 and over needs income of $110,750 or less for the 2026-2027 school year.

What should I do about tax owed before selling an Erie County house?

Work out which level of government you owe, because the answers come from different offices. County liens near foreclosure sit with RPTS. Current town and school tax sits with the town receiver. The RPTS online system will show county amounts, and the tax line at (716) 858-8333 can give an exact payoff.

  1. Look up the parcel on the county's payment site and note every open year, since foreclosure eligibility turns on liens at least two years old.
  2. If the parcel appears on a foreclosure list, find the last day of redemption and answer deadline stated in the notice you received.
  3. Call RPTS to ask whether a payment plan is possible for an owner-occupied home.
  4. Pass the payoff figures to your closing attorney so the lien is cleared at or before closing.

If a house has already been sold at auction, the former owner may be owed surplus money. The county's FAQ says the claimant files a Notice of Claim in the County Clerk's Office and starts a legal proceeding on notice to others with an interest, and that a lawyer is not required. A judge decides who receives what.

Frequently asked questions

How long must an Erie County tax lien go unpaid before foreclosure?

Two years or more. The county's in rem notices state that Erie County may foreclose on tax liens outstanding for that long. In Rem 173 covered liens through tax year 2022.

How much is the Erie County foreclosure fee?

$500, according to the In Rem 173 information sheet. It is paid on top of the unpaid liens and interest and, per the county's FAQ, should be issued as a separate check.

Can I pay Erie County delinquent tax online?

Yes. The county's Pay Your Taxes page says its online system accepts delinquent Erie County property taxes for any town or city in the county, and current county tax for the City of Buffalo. Current bills elsewhere go to the town receiver.

Is there an Erie County foreclosure auction coming up?

The most recent date on the county's page was August 26, 2026 at the Buffalo Convention Center, and it has passed. Call RPTS at (716) 858-8333 for the next schedule and the status of In Rem 174.

Who helps Erie County owners facing tax foreclosure for free?

The New York State Attorney General's Homeowner Protection Program, at 1-855-HOME-456, connects owners to free housing counseling or legal help. The county tells owners to avoid anyone who charges a fee to guarantee foreclosure relief.

Where do I pay and ask about property tax in Monroe County, NY?

In Monroe County, the Treasury Division of the Department of Finance collects fees and taxes at the County Office Building, Room B2, 39 W. Main Street in Rochester, and you can reach it at 585 753-1200. Your town or city tax receiver and your assessor are separate offices, and the county publishes a contact table for both.

Monroe County lies on the southern shore of Lake Ontario, with Rochester as county seat and largest city. The county's own table lists twenty town offices, from Brighton and Chili to Webster and Wheatland, plus the City of Rochester. That is a lot of separate assessors, and each sets values for its own roll, so a house in Pittsford and a house in Greece are assessed by different offices on the same county calendar.

In the City of Rochester, the assessor and the tax receiver both work from City Hall, Room 101-A, at 30 Church Street. Suburban owners deal with their town hall instead, and a few towns share an assessor: the county table shows the same assessor name covering Mendon and East Rochester, and another covering Gates and Ogden.

  • Pay or look up a bill through the county's Real Property Portal, linked from the Treasury page.
  • Ask your town assessor about value, exemptions and Grievance Day.
  • Ask the town or city tax receiver about a bill that has not arrived.

When are Monroe County tax bills due?

The combined town and county bill is mailed by December 31 and is due in full on February 10, or in four installments on February 10, February 28, March 30 and April 30. School bills are mailed by August 31 and are due October 1, with three installment dates of September 15, October 15 and November 15.

The third school installment date, November 15, is today, so a balance left unpaid after it will be treated as unpaid school tax. The county says any unpaid school balance, plus penalty and interest, is re-levied onto the next combined town and county bill. In other words, a school balance you ignore in the fall comes back on the January bill under the county's name.

Owners aged 65 or older, or with a disability, who live in a one- to three-family home can name a trusted adult to receive duplicate bills and unpaid-tax notices. The application deadline each year is November 1, so for 2026 that date has passed.

What happens when Monroe County property tax goes unpaid?

Monroe County runs a long, notice-heavy process that lasts about twenty-eight months before an auction, and it says a signed payment plan in good standing keeps a parcel out of foreclosure. The county's Treasury page lists up to ten notices over that span.

What are the Monroe County assessment and grievance dates?

Town property is valued as of July 1 and taxable status is March 1, the date exemption applications must be filed. The tentative roll is filed May 1, Grievance Day is the fourth Tuesday of May, and the final roll is signed July 1.

For 2027 the fourth Tuesday of May is May 25, but confirm with your local assessor, as the county itself advises. The City of Rochester runs on a different calendar: its valuation date and taxable status date are both February 1, and its tentative roll comes March 1. A seller in Rochester therefore has an earlier window to challenge value than a seller in a suburban town.

Monroe County also posts its tax rate tables online, including 2026 town and county rates, 2025-26 school rates, 2025 village rates and 2026 special district rates. If you suspect you pay too much, compare your rate lines before you decide whether an appeal is worth the effort.

What do Monroe County homes and owners look like?

Monroe County is the most urban of this group, with 750,506 residents in the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate and 342,061 housing units on about 657 square miles of land. Owners occupy 63.7% of homes, so rental properties are a large share of the market.

The median owner-occupied home was valued at $213,700 for 2020 to 2024, median household income was $76,382, and median gross rent was $1,173. Eastman Kodak, Paychex and Wegmans are among the employers tied to the area, and about 25 public school districts serve the county, including the Rochester City School District.

The county-wide median hides wide differences between lakeshore suburbs and Rochester neighborhoods, so check your own parcel's assessment and tax rate lines instead of leaning on the average.

Commutes are short by upstate standards, with mean travel time to work of 19.9 minutes, and the Census counts 318,428 households at 2.28 people each. The Census lists 755 building permits for 2025. A written payoff from the Treasury office gives a buyer or title company a firm number to work from.

How do I sell a Monroe County house with tax owed?

Get a current payoff from the Treasury office, then decide whether to pay it, set up a payment plan or sell before the August 15 publication. The county says staff will try to negotiate a plan during the whole process, and housing counseling agencies such as the Urban League of Rochester and The Housing Council are named on its page.

If a plan is not workable, selling can clear the balance from proceeds. A buyer who pays cash and takes the home in its present condition can shorten the timeline, which helps when a publication date or auction schedule is near.

February 10 is the due date for full payment, with installments due February 10, February 28, March 30 and April 30. The bill is mailed by December 31 to your lender if you escrow, or to you directly.

It is the fourth Tuesday in May in the towns, which is May 25, 2027. The Board of Assessment Review meets then, and it is the last day to file a formal complaint against a tentative assessment. Confirm locally.

Yes. County Treasury staff try to negotiate a plan with owners, and the county says a signed plan with no missed payments keeps a parcel out of foreclosure. Call 585 753-1200 to ask.

When does Monroe County list delinquent properties?

By law the list of lands with unpaid taxes is published on August 15, and the county declares taxes delinquent on August 20. A second publication follows if the balance stays unpaid into the next year.

Where is Onondaga County and which communities does it cover?

Onondaga County sits in the middle of New York State, west of Utica and Albany and east of Rochester, with Syracuse as the county seat. Syracuse is the only city inside the county line. Everything else is a town, a village or a hamlet, which matters because the office that collects your tax depends on where the parcel sits.

The county covers 806 square miles, of which 778 are land, and was split off from Herkimer County in 1794. The north is a flat lake plain crossed by the Erie Canal and its later Barge Canal route, while the south climbs onto the Appalachian Plateau and the Finger Lakes country. Larger places outside the city include Baldwinsville, North Syracuse, Solvay, Manlius and Fayetteville. Interstate 81, the Thruway (Interstate 90), Interstate 690 and U.S. Route 20 are the main roads, and a house near one of them is easier to show to out-of-town buyers.

A cash buyer can take the house as it stands, with the tax debt, repairs and any tenants, which saves an owner who is short on time from preparing the house for a financed buyer. Compare that against listing with an agent, and keep the redemption date in front of you either way.

What kind of place is Oswego County, New York?

Oswego County fills a stretch of the eastern shore of Lake Ontario, north of Syracuse and northwest of Utica. It was formed in 1816 from parts of Oneida and Onondaga Counties, and its name comes from a Mohawk word for the point where the Oswego River pours into the lake. The city of Oswego is both the county seat and its largest city.

The county covers 1,312 square miles, and 360 of those, about 27 percent, are water. The Tug Hill Plateau reaches into the east end and gives the county its high point at 1,550 feet, while the 110 foot Salmon River Falls draws sightseers in the northeast. Oswego Harbor and Port Ontario are the two harbors.

Two cities, Oswego and Fulton, sit among 22 towns. Villages such as Phoenix, Pulaski, Central Square, Mexico and Sandy Creek are spread around Oneida Lake and the lake shore. SUNY Oswego and a Fulton branch campus of Cayuga County Community College, so two colleges are inside the county.

Does lake effect snow matter when selling an Oswego County house?

It can. In February 2007, a lake effect storm dropped more than 10 feet of snow on parts of the county, caused several roof collapses and led to a state of emergency. Roof condition is therefore worth documenting before you list or accept an offer.

If your roof has had repairs, keep the paperwork. If it has not been checked in years, a buyer paying cash and taking the house as-is will not ask you to make repairs first, and you can compare that against what a financed sale would require of you.

Who bills and collects property tax in Oswego County?

The county does not run a single bill. Oswego County describes four separate bills: county and town, city, village and school. The county and town bill is issued January 1, the City of Oswego bill April 1, a Phoenix village bill March 1, other village bills June 1, and school bills in September or, in the Oswego City School District, October.

Local tax collectors take the first payments. Afterward, the County Treasurer is the enforcing officer for unpaid taxes everywhere except the City of Fulton, where the Fulton City Chamberlain enforces city, county and school tax. The county's Real Property Tax Services department, at 46 E. Bridge Street in Oswego, keeps tax maps and the assessment software. It states that it does not set assessments, collect taxes or keep payment receipts. The county's general line is 800-596-3200.

  • Assessments and exemption approvals: your town or city assessor.
  • Payments during the first collection window: the local tax collector named on your bill.
  • Delinquent taxes: the County Treasurer, or the Fulton Chamberlain for Fulton.
  • Deeds and surveys: the County Clerk.

What are the Oswego County tax dates and interest charges?

A county and town bill is due by January 31 without interest, with local collection running to March 31, and unpaid balances are returned to the county in mid-April. Interest is simple during local collection. Under the county's table, a county or town bill adds 1 percent after 30 days and 1 percent for each further month, a village bill adds 5 percent after 30 days, and a school bill adds 2 percent.

County and town bills may be paid in two equal installments unless an escrow account pays them. The first goes to the local collector by March 31, and the second goes to the County Treasurer by June 30 with interest on the remaining balance.

The county also warns that a tax bill that never arrives does not cancel the tax. Property taxes are levied against the land and buildings, so a sale transfers the problem to the buyer unless the balance is paid at closing.

How does an Oswego County tax foreclosure work?

Every property tax becomes a lien on the property and stays one until paid. The county starts Article 11 foreclosure on taxes that remain unpaid two years after they were issued, or four years for agricultural land. It holds two foreclosures each year in that way, and everything it forecloses on is sold together at one auction.

The auction rules are strict. The County Treasurer collects unpaid tax for every property except those in the City of Fulton, where the Fulton City Chamberlain does. Oswego city taxes go to the county one year after the city issues them. The county's general number is 800-596-3200.

How much interest does Oswego County add to a late bill?

During local collection, a county or town bill adds 1 percent after 30 days and 1 percent per further month. A village bill adds 5 percent after 30 days and a school bill adds 2 percent, each followed by 1 percent monthly. After the bill is returned to the county, interest compounds, so ask the Treasurer for the current payoff.

How long before Oswego County forecloses on unpaid taxes?

The county forecloses on taxes unpaid two years after they were issued, and four years for agricultural properties. Foreclosed parcels are sold together at one auction. The redemption period under state law is two years from the lien date unless the tax district sets another.

Can I split my Oswego County tax payment?

No. Your town or city assessor sets the assessment and approves exemptions. The county Real Property Tax Services office keeps tax maps and the assessment software but states that it does not set assessments or collect taxes.

Jefferson County splits the job among town and city assessors, local tax collectors and two county offices in Watertown. How do I pay a Jefferson County tax bill?

Start with a call to the Treasurer. The Treasurer's page asks owners to verify the amount and the collector at 315-785-3055 or treasurer@jeffersoncountyny.gov before paying, and it will reject and return a payment sent for the wrong amount or to the wrong collector.

Treasurer hours are 9 am to 5 pm from September 1 through June 30, with collections until 4:45 pm. In July and August the hours are 8:30 am to 4 pm. In 2026 the Treasurer began accepting full town and county payments on March 13, so ask for the current year's opening date.

How do I challenge an assessment in Jefferson County?

File Form RP-524 with the assessor or Board of Assessment Review in your town or city by Grievance Day. New York State says that day is the fourth Tuesday in May in most communities, and that you should confirm it with your local assessor or municipal clerk. In 2027 the fourth Tuesday is May 25.

Filing is free and needs no lawyer. Only the assessment on the current tentative roll can be grieved. If the board turns you down, an owner-occupied home qualifies for Small Claims Assessment Review at $30, started within 30 days after the final roll is filed. Villages that assess their own property keep separate dates, usually in February, so a village homeowner may have two assessments to check.

The county office can help local assessors on valuations, small claims hearings and rolls, while the local board hears the grievance itself. Call Real Property Tax Services at 315-785-3074 with questions about a parcel's tax map or address.

What happens when Jefferson County taxes go unpaid?

The county can foreclose, and its own FAQ describes how to stop it. A parcel is saved by paying every delinquent tax, interest, penalty and fee before the redemption date, or by signing an installment agreement for owners who qualify.

  • An installment agreement requires 25% down on all delinquent amounts for the owner's county properties outside Watertown, then eight roughly equal quarterly payments over two years, with new taxes paid in full and on time.
  • An owner is eligible once at least 30 days late, but not after defaulting on an earlier agreement or losing property to foreclosure within three years.
  • State law requires redeeming the newest taxes first, so paying only the oldest year does not remove a parcel from the list.
  • Deadlines are firm, and the county says extensions are not possible. Only a majority vote of the County Legislature can waive penalties and interest.

Once the county takes title at foreclosure, the former owner's interest ends. The county generally offers the property at its annual tax auction, selling as-is by quitclaim deed, and an auction buyer takes on the school and village tax for the auction year. Tax liens follow the property, so a buyer inherits the bill even if the seller never mentions it. Three steps help. Ask the town, village or school collector for the current-year status. Ask the Treasurer for the delinquent balance with interest through the closing date. Tell the title company about any installment agreement so the remaining balance is paid off at closing. A third party who pays your tax does not gain the house, since the county says the old tax sale certificate practice ended years ago.

An owner who inherited a home in Le Ray, Clayton or Adams and fell behind does not have to wait for an auction. A cash sale can bring the tax current in one closing.

What is the Jefferson County housing market like?

Jefferson County sits on New York's northern border at the point where the St. Lawrence River leaves Lake Ontario. It was founded in 1805, has Watertown as county seat, and covers 1,269 square miles of land. The Black River drains through it, the Tug Hill Plateau rises in the south, and part of the Thousand Islands lies within its borders. Le Ray is the largest town, with a 2020 count of 25,574, and the Fort Drum base is home to the Army's 10th Mountain Division.

Median household income is $66,301, the typical commute is 19.5 minutes, and the county counts 9,861 veterans. School districts include Carthage, Indian River, Watertown, General Brown, South Jefferson and Thousand Islands.

Villages include Carthage, West Carthage, Clayton, Adams, Sackets Harbor, Alexandria Bay and Cape Vincent, and Jefferson Community College is in Watertown. Summer tourism lifts the population noticeably, so a listing that sits through the winter can look different in July. Ask the County Treasurer for a payoff letter that runs through your expected closing date, since interest keeps accruing until the day the money arrives.

The County Treasurer collects delinquent village, school, town and county real property tax, except in the City of Watertown. The office is at 175 Arsenal Street in Watertown, 315-785-3055.

Can I get an extension on Jefferson County foreclosure deadlines?

No. The county's FAQ says all deadlines are firm. The only ways to save the property are paying everything owed before the redemption date or entering an installment agreement.

How does a Jefferson County installment agreement work?

You pay 25% of all delinquent taxes, interest, fees and penalties up front, then eight roughly equal quarterly payments over two years. You must also keep all new taxes current.

When is Grievance Day in Jefferson County?

In most New York communities it is the fourth Tuesday in May, which is May 25 in 2027. Confirm the date with your town or city assessor, since villages and some cities differ.

Does paying someone else's delinquent tax give me their Jefferson County property?

No. The county says the sale of tax certificates ended years ago, and ownership stays with the owner of record no matter who pays.

Who bills and collects property tax in Wayne County, NY?

The town tax collector sends and collects your combined town and county bill, and the Wayne County Treasurer in Lyons takes over a bill that is still unpaid after March. Wayne County has no cities. It has 15 towns and seven villages on the south shore of Lake Ontario, between Rochester and Syracuse, and Lyons is the county seat.

The county's Real Property Tax Services Agency works behind the scenes. Its 2024 annual report says it produces the assessment rolls, tax rolls and tax bills for the towns, villages and school districts, keeps the tax maps, investigates correction-of-error requests, divides the county levy among the assessing jurisdictions and calculates tax rates. It also supplies bills to 22 school districts, some of which lie outside the county.

When are Wayne County property taxes due?

Town and County bills are issued by each town around January 1 and are payable to the town collector in January, February and March. The county's Taxpayers Guide sets the cost of waiting: nothing extra in January, 1 percent added in February and 2 percent added in March.

The tax year runs from January 1 to December 31. The Treasurer's FAQ says an owner can pay current taxes in two payments. The first falls due by the end of the penalty-free period, and the second is due in February or March with interest added. The same FAQ warns that a buyer who closed after March 1 will not receive a bill until the next billing cycle, and that the owner remains responsible for paying on time even when no bill arrives.

Rural fire, rural light and rural water or sewer charges can appear on a bill as special assessments, so a parcel in the countryside may carry lines that a village lot does not. Your bill is the taxable assessment multiplied by the rate, plus those special charges.

What happens when Wayne County taxes go unpaid?

On April 1 the town bill is treated as delinquent and goes to the County Treasurer, and the county can foreclose when taxes stay unpaid for two years. The Taxpayers Guide describes a ladder of added costs once the Treasurer holds the bill.

  • April 1: the bill moves to the Treasurer, and the guide mentions a 25 percent penalty at transfer.

  • March, tentatively: the last chance to redeem before foreclosure, followed by a public auction of unpaid parcels in June.

The Treasurer's FAQ describes a payment program for eligible owners. It is available for delinquent taxes after June 1, runs up to 24 months and needs a down payment of at least 10 percent. Call the office before any step above, because the payoff changes every month.

State law sets the outer frame. Under RPTL 1110 a delinquent lien can be redeemed by paying the amount due plus legal charges before the redemption period ends, normally two years after the lien date. The county's 2024 report adds that a 2024 change to Article 11 now returns surplus proceeds of a tax sale to the former owner. The county held its 2024 online auction from May 30 to June 19 with about 15 parcels, and the Treasurer's office handles sales from now on.

Owners of one-, two- and three-family owner-occupied homes can go on to a Small Claims Assessment Review hearing. Anyone may file a certiorari petition in Supreme Court. The county's policy, adopted by the Board of Supervisors in 1995, is that it learns of a case only when the assessed value reaches $1,000,000, the threshold for county participation. Working orchards and fields can qualify for an agricultural assessment, and Wayne County has a lot of it. Wayne County had an estimated 91,250 residents in July 2025 and 43,064 housing units. Owners occupy 79.9 percent of homes, which is a high share, and the median owner-occupied home is valued at $170,000 for 2020 to 2024.

Median gross rent is $938, median household income is $74,506, and the county covers 603.83 square miles of land. Largest town by population is Arcadia, and Newark is the biggest village. These are countywide medians, so a lake-view property in Sodus Point and a village house in Clyde can differ widely.

What should I do before selling a Wayne County house with tax due?

Get a written payoff from the right office for each layer of tax, because the town collector, the Treasurer, the village and the school district each hold different pieces. A short list keeps the closing on schedule.

  • Call the Treasurer at 315-946-7441 if any bill went past April 1, and ask for the figure including penalties, interest and any enforcement fee.

Two years of unpaid taxes. The Treasurer's FAQ says the county can foreclose when taxes remain unpaid for two years, and the Taxpayers Guide places the public auction in June and the tentative last redemption date in March.

You will not get a bill until the next billing cycle, but you are still responsible for paying on time. Ask the town tax collector for the amount before the penalty-free period ends.

Interest on unpaid town and county tax starts February 1 at 1% per month. School tax follows its own path. The county explains that the school tax collector sends the Treasurer a list of unpaid school taxes on or before November 15, which means a school balance can join the county's delinquent file a few weeks from today.

What penalty applies after April 30 in Madison County?

A 5% county return penalty is added to the original tax once the balance goes back to the Treasurer, and interest continues at 1% per month. A town notice fee may also apply if the town charges one.

When is the Madison County property auction?

The county generally holds its auction in September of the third year of delinquency, usually on the third Saturday. The Board of Supervisors then typically votes on the sales in October. Ask the Treasurer for the current year's date.

Does missing the tax bill stop interest?

No. The county states that interest and penalties are not waived because a taxpayer did not receive a bill. Contact the local tax collector if a bill has not arrived within a week of issue.

Can I still file an exemption this year?

Exemption forms are due to your assessor by March 1, or May 1 in the City of Oneida, and that date has passed for 2026. The next deadline is March 1, 2027, and the forms are on the state tax department website.

Who collects property tax in Fulton County, New York?

Town collectors take current county and town tax early in the year, and the Fulton County Treasurer takes over anything left unpaid. The Treasurer's office is in the County Office Building at 223 West Main Street, Room 202, Johnstown, NY 12095, phone (518) 736-5580. Its hours are Monday to Friday, 9 am to 5 pm, shortened to 4 pm from July 1 through Labor Day.

Per the county's own description, the Treasurer collects delinquent school, village, town and county taxes, runs the foreclosure and auction process under the state Real Property Tax Law, and works with the town tax collectors. It also collects and enforces taxes on parcels in the City of Gloversville, and the page says it does not collect City of Johnstown taxes.

The Real Property Tax Service Agency, at (518) 736-5507 in the same building, was created under Article 15-A of the state Real Property Tax Law in 1970 and maintains the tax maps. Its online Beacon map shows ownership, property inventory and assessed value, refreshed nightly, and explains the parcel's SBL (section, block, lot) number that appears on tax bills and assessment rolls.

What is the Fulton County tax calendar?

Each tax has its own window, and the Treasurer's payments page spells them out. The county and town windows are early in the year, school and village windows come in the fall, and the City of Gloversville has its own calendar.

Village and school payments are not accepted after October 31, and unpaid town school and village amounts are relevied on the next county bill. Current county tax cannot be paid during the first two weeks of April while the books transfer, so call the Treasurer in the last week of April for the amount due. The Treasurer's office takes online payments for delinquent town tax at the end of April, and mailed payments go to P.O. Box 128, Johnstown, NY 12095, never as cash.

Can I pay delinquent Fulton County taxes in installments?

Possibly, but only in May. Local Law No. 2 of 1997 lets the Treasurer sign installment agreements with owners of residential real property, and the county processes them only from May 1 through May 31. Letters go out in April to qualified owners who are behind.

  • The down payment is 25% of the eligible delinquent taxes.
  • Payments are monthly, and the term cannot exceed 24 months.

  • Commercial property and land are not eligible.
  • A parcel foreclosed on within the last three years, or one that defaulted on an installment agreement in the last three years, is not eligible.

The county page directs owners to call the Treasurer to confirm whether they qualify. The May 2026 window has closed, so the next chance is May 2027.

Owners could pay at the Treasurer's office or by card online. The page also pointed people toward the New York State Homeowner Assistance Fund for help with delinquent taxes. What is Fulton County like for homeowners?

Fulton County is in the Mohawk Valley, with Johnstown as the county seat and Gloversville as the largest city. It was formed on April 18, 1838, from part of Montgomery County. About 58% of its 533 square miles lies inside Adirondack Park. Gloves and leather were the main industry for generations, and few glovers and tanners remain today.

Hamilton County is to the north, Saratoga to the east, Montgomery to the south and Herkimer to the west. State routes 10, 29, 30 and 67 are among the main roads. School districts include Gloversville City, Johnstown City, Broadalbin-Perth, Mayfield, Northville and Galway, and Fulton-Montgomery Community College is in Johnstown. The old Tryon County courthouse of 1772 in Johnstown is now the Fulton County Courthouse and is described as New York's oldest operating courthouse. Population has slipped from 55,531 in 2010 to an estimated 52,216 in 2025, and only 85 building permits were recorded in 2025, which is a small number for a county with more than 28,000 housing units. The county's parcel records, searchable through the Beacon map, are the place to check ownership, inventory and assessed value for any house before it is listed.

How do I clear Fulton County tax before closing a sale?

Ask the right office for the right year. The Real Property Tax Service Agency says that during tax collection dates you contact the local tax collector, and outside those dates you contact the County Treasurer for county and town taxes and the city or school collector for those taxes.

  1. Find the parcel's SBL number on the Beacon map or the tax bill.
  2. Call the Treasurer at (518) 736-5580 and ask for a Parcel Status Report on any delinquent year.
  3. Pay older years first, since the Treasurer requires reverse chronological order for foreclosure redemption.
  4. Ask about exemptions, STAR and veteran or senior benefits through your assessor or the county's real property office at (518) 736-5509. STAR applications go to the state directly.
  5. Give the closing attorney the written payoff amounts.

January 1 through March 31. After that the town collector returns unpaid bills to the County Treasurer, and the Treasurer's office begins collections on May 1.

Is there a Fulton County installment plan for back taxes?

Yes, for eligible owners of residential property, but agreements are processed only in May. The down payment is 25% of the eligible delinquent tax, the term is up to 24 months, and payments are monthly.

No. The Treasurer's page says it does not collect City of Johnstown taxes, though it does collect City of Gloversville parcels. For Johnstown, contact the city.

Use the Beacon online map from the Real Property Tax Service Agency. It shows the SBL, also called the tax map number, along with ownership and assessed value. The same number appears on tax bills and assessment rolls.

Apply directly with New York State. The Real Property Tax Service Agency's page says owners now register with the state, and gives (518) 457-2036 as the state number.

Which Montgomery County office handles delinquent property tax?

The Montgomery County Treasurer handles delinquent taxes, from the County Annex Building at 20 Park Street in Fonda (mailing address PO Box 1500, Fonda, NY 12068). The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM, and the phone number on the county's contact page is 518-853-8175.

  • Assessment, tax roll or rate question: Real Property Tax Department.
  • Value dispute: your town or city assessor and its Board of Assessment Review.

What kind of place is Montgomery County, NY?

Montgomery County is a Mohawk Valley county with Fonda as its seat, bordering the Mohawk River and the Erie Canal corridor west of Schenectady and northwest of Albany. The Census Bureau lists about 403 square miles of land and a July 2025 population estimate of 50,046, up 1.0% from the 2020 base.

The county has ten towns: Amsterdam, Canajoharie, Charleston, Florida, Glen, Minden, Mohawk, Palatine, Root and St. Johnsville. The City of Amsterdam sits inside it, along with villages such as Fort Plain, Fultonville, Canajoharie and Palatine Bridge. Under a charter approved by voters in 2012, the county has had an elected county executive and a nine-member legislature since January 2014.

Housing is inexpensive here. The median owner-occupied home was valued at $157,500 for 2020 to 2024, owners occupy 70.4% of homes, median household income is $64,943 and 15.5% of residents are in poverty. At those prices, a few years of back tax, interest and fees can take a big bite out of what a seller nets.

The Census counts 19,603 households at 2.46 people each and 23,243 housing units, with median gross rent of $940 and a mean commute of 24.0 minutes. Only 105 building permits were issued in 2025, so the county has little new construction competing with resale homes. A buyer who accepts the home as it stands removes the repair question from the sale, leaving the tax payoff as the main item to settle.

How does the City of Amsterdam calendar differ from the towns?

The City of Amsterdam assesses on a winter schedule that runs ahead of the towns by months. Its valuation date and taxable status date are both December 1, the tentative roll is filed January 1, and the final roll is filed March 1.

The county's page then gives the city's judicial deadlines: a small claims assessment review application and an Article 7 certiorari filing are both due March 31, which is 30 days after the final roll is filed. Use these postings to check your parcel before you list. A seller who looks up the roll in May and the rate in January can estimate the next bill with real numbers, rather than guessing from last year's.

How can I sell a Montgomery County home with property tax owed?

Call the Treasurer in Fonda and ask for a payoff figure on your parcel, then compare it with an offer. The county's treasurer page invites questions about delinquent taxes, and the redemption rule in state law gives you a defined period to pay. Under RPTL 1110, a property with a delinquent lien can be redeemed by paying the lien and the charges authorized by law, and the period ends two years after the lien date unless the published notice names a later date.

A sale that pays cash and accepts the house as it stands can close faster than a retail listing, which matters when you want the balance cleared before it grows. In a county where the median home is valued near $157,500, fast action keeps fees from outrunning your equity.

The same logic applies if you plan to contest value before selling. The state notes there is no cost to grieve and no need for a lawyer, and that you can only challenge the assessment on the current tentative roll, not past years.
